django_fileresponse (link to documentation) is a library that allows you to serve files directly from Django.

Features of django_fileresponse

django_fileresponse provides the following features for developers:

  • Use asyncio to serve files with high concurrency directly from Django.
  • Uses aiofiles to asynchronously read from filesystem and aiobotocore to asynchronously read from s3 compatible object stores

Streaming memory is proportional to the chunk size; emitted payloads are not retained. Each send is awaited before reading again, so slow clients apply backpressure. All response classes accept chunk_size as an integer from 1 through 1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB), default 4096. Invalid values, including booleans, raise ValueError before opening a stream or sending headers.

Responses expose Django's async StreamingHttpResponse interface, including is_async and streaming_content, so GZipMiddleware and other async streaming middleware can transform their content. The custom handler sends the wrapped iterator and closes the original file or S3 body/client promptly on cancellation or read/send failure. ASGI header names are lowercase; header values and separate cookies are preserved.

Legacy custom adapters that call send_stream_to_client(stream, send) from stream(send) also send middleware-transformed content; they retain ownership of their already-open resource context. Each response is single-use.

Installing

django_fileresponse is on PyPI so you can just run pip install django_fileresponse.

Replace Default ASGIHandler

Use AsyncFileASGIHandler to send middleware-wrapped async content and ensure prompt cleanup of the original filesystem or S3 resource when streaming fails or the client disconnects.

So instead of building your application like this:

{% raw %} 
from django.core.asgi import get_asgi_application

application = get_asgi_application()
{% endraw %}

You have to import a modified ASGIHandler from fileresponse:

{% raw %} 
from fileresponse.asgi import get_asgi_application

application = get_asgi_application()
{% endraw %}

If you use a different mechanism to launch your application, you could also just import the modified AsyncFileASGIHandler directly:

{% raw %} 
from fileresponse.handlers import AsyncFileASGIHandler

django.setup(set_prefix=False)
application = AsyncFileASGIHandler()
{% endraw %}

How to use Async Fileresponses in your Views

Add functions below to your views.py

Serving from Filesystem

{% raw %} 
from fileresponse.http import AiofileFileResponse as AiofileFileResponse


async def get_file(request, path):
    file_path = Path(path)
    return AiofileFileResponse(file_path)
{% endraw %}

Serve Files from an S3 Compatible Object Store

{% raw %} 
from fileresponse.http import AiobotocoreFileResponse


async def get_file(request, key):
    bucket = settings.FILERESPONSE_S3_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME
    return AiobotocoreFileResponse(bucket, key, chunk_size=4096)
{% endraw %}

Settings

Example Settings for an S3 Compatible Object Store 

FILERESPONSE_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID="minioadmin"
FILERESPONSE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="minioadmin"
FILERESPONSE_S3_REGION="us-west-2"
FILERESPONSE_S3_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME="fileresponse"
FILERESPONSE_S3_ENDPOINT_URL="http://localhost:9000"

Alternatively pass endpoint_url, region_name, aws_access_key_id, secret_access_key and use_ssl to AiobotocoreFileResponse. These option names are unchanged; secret_access_key becomes the client aws_secret_access_key. Explicit values bypass their individual S3 settings. All four endpoint/region/credential values must be supplied either as overrides or Django settings; missing settings raise ImproperlyConfigured before network access. use_ssl defaults to False when neither option nor setting is supplied. Django itself must still be configured.

Development and validation

The supported toolchain is CPython 3.11–3.13, Django 5.2, aiofiles 24.1–25.x, and aiobotocore 2.21–2.x. The development extra pins nbdev 1.2.11 and its compatible conversion dependencies; nbdev 2 uses a different notebook format. The package version is unchanged.

In a virtual environment, install python -m pip install -e '.[dev]', then run:

ruff check fileresponse tests scripts
mypy fileresponse scripts
python scripts/generate.py --check
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python -m build
python scripts/package_smoke.py

CI runs these checks on every supported Python version with read-only repository permissions. Tests generate synthetic bytes and temporary files, fake S3 clients, and verify memory bounds, backpressure, chunk validation, ASGI handling, and client/body cleanup. They need no object-store settings, credentials, or services. The package smoke test installs both wheel and sdist in fresh environments and runs the same suite outside the checkout. Remove old dist/ artifacts before rebuilding so it contains exactly one wheel and one sdist.

Edit nbs/*.ipynb, then run python scripts/generate.py --docs to regenerate Python, README and API HTML. Generation uses a disposable copy, preserves the published documentation base URL, and executes only import/show_doc cells for API documentation. --check verifies the generated Python and README without changing the checkout; add --docs to check API HTML too. The MinIO, sample project and concurrent-download demonstrations are excluded from mandatory CI and documentation execution.
